raw.retained_raw_text: {"schema_version":"chat_response_v1","response_type":"answer","answer_text":"The light-dependent reactions convert light energy into chemical energy stored in energy carriers, which then travel to the Calvin cycle. Photosystems absorb light and use electron transport chains to convert energy into the chemical energy of ATP and NADPH [ev_002]. The overall purpose of the light-dependent reactions is to convert light energy into chemical energy, and this chemical energy will be used by the Calvin cycle to fuel the assembly of sugar molecules [ev_008]. The energy-carrying molecules ATP and NADPH travel into the stroma, where the Calvin cycle reactions take place [ev_007]. The carriers that move energy from the light-dependent reactions to the Calvin cycle are described as \"full\" because they bring energy; after the energy is released, the \"empty\" carriers return to the light-dependent reactions to obtain more energy [ev_001].
